_comment: VOICE RULES — the wording the methodology forbids, checked rather than
merely requested.
These are transcribed from the hard rules in the live system's prompts,
where they exist only as instructions. The model is told not to write
"foster" or "You are not alone"; nothing has ever verified that it didn't.
That is the same gap that let the professional-help sequence be honoured
intermittently — and unlike that one, these failures are invisible even on
close reading, because a plan full of "facilitate" and "holistic" still
looks like a plan.
TWO THINGS TO KNOW BEFORE ADDING A TERM:
1. RESOURCE TITLES ARE STRIPPED BEFORE CHECKING. Three of the banned
words below appear inside approved workshop titles — "Engagement" in
the Effective Communication workshop, "Dynamics" in Family Dynamics,
"Reinforcement" in Positive Reinforcement. Without stripping, every
correctly-cited report would be flagged, and a checker that cries wolf
gets switched off. Required wording is stripped for the same reason.
2. `words` MATCH ON WORD BOUNDARIES, `phrases` MATCH ANYWHERE. So the word
"reinforce" does not fire on "reinforcement" appearing in prose, while
the phrase "wait and see" fires wherever it appears. Pick `kind`
accordingly: a stem you want to catch in all its forms belongs in
`phrases`.
Strictness `retry` regenerates the report and feeds the error back. `warn`
logs and ships. Everything here is a content edit.

rules.reason: These read as a consultant's report rather than someone who has sat with families. The methodology bans them outright.
Polished empathy in place of a concrete observation. A parent who has just described their child's secrecy does not need to be told they are not alone; they need to be told what to do on Tuesday.

en: I hear how hard this is
es: escucho lo difícil que es esto

rules.reason: Not part of this methodology. Building the network around the child belongs to the Essential Workshop "Building a Support Network"; co-parent alignment uses co-parent or co-guardian. The generic instruction sends a parent nowhere in particular.

Drug exposure now includes pressed pills, powders, counterfeit prescriptions, vape cartridges and edibles. Naming pills alone narrows a parent's vigilance to the one thing they have already thought of.
The parent administers the test. "Take a drug test" as the parent's action reads as the parent testing themselves.

At these severities the methodology requires a named next move. "See how it goes" is what a parent does instead of acting, and offering it as the recommendation is how a serious situation gets a week older.

en: circle back when things calm down
es: vuelve cuando las cosas se calmen

rules.reason: At MODERATE the methodology names these two specifically: every priority area must end in a concrete commitment, so an ending of "see how it goes" with no named next move is the one thing it must not be. The wider list belongs to SERIOUS.
ASAP philosophy is that consequences alone do not change behaviour, so rewards and consequences travel together. These exact formulations are the ones that arrive without their pair.

es: aplica las consecuencias de forma consistente

rules.reason: Softening a referral into a future task erases it. The recommendation is direct, and the professional-help sequence follows it.

es: empieza a pensar en un terapeuta

rules.reason: A meta-reference in place of required wording is a failure, not a shortcut. Every one of these has been produced by a model at some point in place of the actual sentences.

es: agrega la secuencia de dos oraciones

_comment: The questionnaire's option labels are intake-form text, not speech.
Quoting one back — 'your "Near-daily — running on empty" exhaustion' — is
the clearest tell that a plan was assembled from a form rather than
written about a family.
Only the labels the parent actually chose are checked, and only those with
at least `minWords` words: a short label like "Drug Testing" or "Always
consistent" occurs in ordinary prose and would fire constantly.
